description: Add the artifacts that explicitly DEMONSTRATE each of the seven required Kiro University final-exam lessons (plus the two bonuses) and a top-level DEMONSTRATED_LESSONS.md that explains to the judges how each lesson was demonstrated with references to the relevant repo files. The seven lessons: (1) Spec-driven development, (2) Steering docs, (3) Hooks, (4) Property-based testing (IDE-only), (5) Powers, (6) Model Context Protocol (MCP), (7) Custom Agents. Bonuses: Kiro Web / cloud sessions / cloud configuration writeup, and packaging a Kiro Power. Code-backed lessons (specs tie to real modules; property-based tests exercise real functions) must actually run; doc-only lessons must be accurate and reference real files.
steps: LESSON 1 - Spec-driven development: create .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/requirements.md (EARS-style user stories + acceptance criteria covering the bracket view, win/loss prediction, Bedrock narrative, data strategy, deploy), design.md (architecture: React/Vite SPA on S3+CloudFront, API Gateway + Lambda, DynamoDB cache, Bedrock, CDK; component/sequence descriptions grounded in the ACTUAL code - bracketService resolution order, aggregateBracket, predict, generateNarrative, handlers, the stack), and tasks.md (an implementation task breakdown that maps to the real FEAT-001..FEAT-006 work and the files that implement it). These must describe the real system, not a hypothetical one.

LESSON 2 - Steering: the four .kiro/steering/*.md already exist (kiro-university.md, product.md, tech.md, structure.md with inclusion: always). Verify them and, if helpful, add a short steering file documenting testing conventions (unit + property-based + Playwright e2e). Reference these in the lessons doc.

LESSON 3 - Hooks: create .kiro/hooks/ with at least two agent hooks in Kiro's hook JSON format (filename pattern *.kiro.hook). Suggested: (a) a hook that runs the backend/shared unit tests when a backend or shared source file is saved; (b) a hook that runs typecheck (npm run typecheck) on save of any .ts/.tsx; optionally (c) a manual hook that runs the Playwright e2e suite. Use the documented Kiro hook schema (enabled, name, description, version, when/then with type and the prompt or command). Keep them valid JSON and self-describing. Document what each hook does in the lessons doc.

LESSON 4 - Property-based testing (IDE-only): add fast-check as a backend devDependency and write property-based tests that exercise REAL functions. At minimum: for predict(series, bracket) assert the invariant that favoriteWinProbability is always within [0.5, 0.95] and favoriteTeamId is always one of the two series teams, across randomly generated series (random team ids, win counts within bestOf, random winPct). For aggregateBracket, generate random valid raw-game arrays and assert structural invariants (each series' high/low wins never exceed bestOf; status is one of the allowed values; league/round always valid). Place as backend/src/**/*.property.test.ts (or similar) so `npm test -w backend` runs them. They must pass and genuinely use fast-check's generators (fc.assert/fc.property).

LESSON 5 - Powers: document how Kiro Powers were used in this build (agent-browser/Playwright power for e2e UI testing, github-cli power for repo/PR). For the BONUS 'package a Kiro Power', create a small self-contained Kiro Power package under a tools/ or powers/ directory in the repo: a power manifest + a steering doc + (optionally) a tiny MCP server or CLI skill, structured per Kiro's power packaging convention, that is relevant to this project (e.g., an 'mlb-postseason' power bundling the MLB Stats API steering + a helper skill). Include a README in the power dir explaining how to install/use it. Keep it buildable/valid; do not break the root build.

LESSON 6 - MCP: create .kiro/settings/mcp.json configuring at least one MCP server relevant to the project (e.g., an AWS documentation MCP server and/or a fetch/HTTP MCP server used to consult the MLB Stats API or AWS docs). Use the documented Kiro MCP config schema (mcpServers map with command, args, env, disabled, autoApprove). Choose servers that are real/installable (e.g., uvx-based awslabs AWS docs server, or a Node fetch server) and document their purpose. Do not require secrets; mark any that need credentials as disabled with a note.

LESSON 7 - Custom Agents: add a custom agent configuration under .kiro/ following Kiro's custom-agent convention (e.g., .kiro/agents/<name>.json or the documented location) defining a project-specific agent persona for this repo (name, description, instructions/system prompt, allowed tools, and any steering/context wiring). Make it coherent with the project (e.g., an 'mlb-postseason-dev' agent that knows the stack and conventions). Document it in the lessons doc.

BONUS A - Kiro Web / cloud sessions / cloud configuration: add a doc (e.g., docs/kiro-web-cloud.md) explaining how the project was built using Kiro Web and cloud sessions, and the local-vs-cloud engineering differences to highlight in the demo video (per the user's note), including how AWS cloud configuration/credentials activate in a new Kiro Web session for cdk deploy. Reference the one-command deploy flow.
BONUS B - Package a Kiro Power: covered by the power package created in LESSON 5 step; ensure it is a self-contained, documented, installable power and note it as the bonus deliverable.

Create DEMONSTRATED_LESSONS.md at the repo root (the '実証された教訓' document for the judges): one section per lesson (1-7) + the two bonuses, each stating HOW the lesson is demonstrated and linking the relevant repo files/paths (relative links). Keep it accurate - every referenced file must exist. Add a short pointer to it from README.md.

Verify nothing broke: run `npm run build`, `npm test` (backend now includes fast-check property tests, plus frontend + infra), and `npm run synth`; all must pass. Validate every .kiro JSON artifact (hooks, mcp.json, agent config) parses as valid JSON. Confirm every file path referenced in DEMONSTRATED_LESSONS.md exists. Commit with clear messages so progress is visible.
acceptance_criteria: DEMONSTRATED_LESSONS.md exists at the repo root with a section for each of the 7 required lessons and the 2 bonuses, each explaining how it was demonstrated and referencing real repo files (all referenced paths exist).
LESSON 1: .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/{requirements.md,design.md,tasks.md} exist and describe the ACTUAL implemented system.
LESSON 3: .kiro/hooks/ contains at least two valid *.kiro.hook JSON files using Kiro's hook schema.

LESSON 4: fast-check property-based tests exist and run under `npm test -w backend`, asserting real invariants of predict() and aggregateBracket() (probability in [0.5,0.95]; favorite is one of the two teams; win counts <= bestOf; valid status/league/round).
LESSON 6: .kiro/settings/mcp.json exists and is valid JSON configuring at least one real MCP server with documented purpose.
LESSON 7: a custom agent configuration exists under .kiro/ (valid JSON) defining a project-specific agent.
BONUS: a self-contained, documented Kiro Power package exists in the repo (manifest + steering/skill + README), and a Kiro Web/cloud-sessions writeup exists.
`npm run build`, `npm test`, and `npm run synth` all pass; every .kiro JSON artifact parses as valid JSON.
verification: From repo root: `npm test` exits 0 (backend incl. fast-check property tests, frontend, infra).
From repo root: `npm run build` and `npm run synth` exit 0.
Validate JSON: every file under .kiro/hooks/, .kiro/settings/mcp.json, and the custom agent config parse as valid JSON.
Confirm DEMONSTRATED_LESSONS.md exists and every repo path it references resolves to a real file.
findings:
Implemented all 7 lessons + 2 bonuses. Files added per lesson:
- Lesson 1 (specs): .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/{requirements.md,design.md,tasks.md} grounded in real code (bracketService resolution order, aggregateBracket, predict, generateNarrative).
- Lesson 2 (steering): verified existing 4 .kiro/steering/*.md; added .kiro/steering/testing.md (inclusion: always).
- Lesson 3 (hooks): .kiro/hooks/run-tests-on-save.kiro.hook, typecheck-on-save.kiro.hook, run-e2e-suite.kiro.hook (valid JSON, enabled/name/description/version/when/then shape).
- Lesson 4 (property-based): added fast-check@^4 as backend devDependency; backend/src/predict/model.property.test.ts and backend/src/mlb/aggregate.property.test.ts. NOTE: initial aggregate generator allowed more games than gamesInSeries, violating wins<=bestOf; fixed by bounding generated game count to gamesInSeries (realistic). Backend now 31 tests pass.
- Lesson 5 + Bonus B (powers): powers/mlb-postseason/ (power.json manifest, steering/mlb-stats-api.md, skills/aggregate-bracket.md, README.md); kept OUTSIDE npm workspaces so root build is unaffected.
- Lesson 6 (MCP): .kiro/settings/mcp.json with aws-docs (uvx awslabs.aws-documentation-mcp-server) and fetch (uvx mcp-server-fetch).
- Lesson 7 (custom agents): .kiro/agents/mlb-postseason-dev.json.
- Bonus A: docs/kiro-web-cloud.md.
- Judge doc: DEMONSTRATED_LESSONS.md at repo root (bilingual JP/EN) + README.md pointer. All referenced paths verified to exist.
Verification: npm run build, npm test (backend 31 incl property, frontend 12, infra 6), npm run synth all exit 0. All .kiro JSON artifacts parse. Committed in 5 scoped commits. Left pre-existing uncommitted items (task.json, infra/bin/app.ts, review .md files, FEAT-005.json) untouched as instructed.
